races.title: Ban on data centers (initiated ordinance)
races.target_project: Project Milo (near Deer Creek Golf Course)
races.summary: Citizen-initiated ordinance prohibiting the construction of any data center within city limits, including converting existing buildings. No megawatt threshold: the only outright ban among Ohio's November measures. Council had already adopted a 12-month moratorium.
races.ballot_text: Shall the ordinance to approve or reject a ban on data centers within the city limits, be passed? (Ohio Secretary of State listing and Trumbull County BOE running list.) The ordinance defines a data center as "any facility that primarily contains electronic equipment used to process, store, and transmit digital information" and also bars converting an existing building into one (fragment per WKBN; full ordinance text not retrieved).
races.notes: Issue number not yet confirmed; check Trumbull BOE sample ballot. Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file.

races.title: Charter amendment banning data centers over 7.5 MW
races.target_project: Thor Equities proposal south of Rittal
races.proponents: Conserve Ohio / Nicole Nawman petition (400+ signatures)
races.summary: Adds Section 8.07 to Article VIII of the city charter prohibiting construction of data centers in the city, with an exemption for small privately owned facilities serving a single organization with peak demand under 7.5 MW. Council rescinded its data-center zoning allowance in June and adopted a 12-month moratorium; Thor Equities sued in federal court. A recall of the mayor is on the same ballot.
races.ballot_text: City of Urbana, Proposed Charter Amendment. A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall Article VIII of the Charter of the City of Urbana be amended to add Section 8.07, to read as follows? Article VIII, Section 8.07. Prohibition of a Data Center. (A) the construction of a data center is hereby prohibited. (B) as used in this Section, "construction" shall mean the erection of one or more buildings, infrastructure, facilities and related activities, which include preparations and modifications for same, for a common purpose. (C) as used in this Section, "data center" shall mean one or more buildings or physical facilities or infrastructure, located on a single real property parcel or on contiguous, adjacent, or otherwise aggregated real property parcels that are used primarily or exclusively for digital information services such as the management, storage, processing and dissemination of electronic data and information, including but not limited to the implementation of artificial intelligence, through the use of computer systems, servers, networking equipment, and related components, including equipment cooling systems, or virtual currency mining. (D) this Section shall not apply to data centers, as defined in this section, whose sole purpose is to serve as a dedicated facility that supports the computing needs of a single organization or enterprise not otherwise engaged in the business of management, storage, processing, and/or dissemination of electronic data and information and which is wholly owned by that enterprise, and which has an aggregate monthly demand or peak load of less than seven-point-five (7.5) megawatts, however derived from any energy source, or a combination thereof. (E) this Section is self-executing. YES / NO
races.notes: Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file as Charter Amendment: Article VII, Section 8.07 (the petition's Article VII/VIII inconsistency carries through to the state list). Full text from the Champaign County sample ballot (Urbana 3-A), which prints it without an issue number; the ballot reads Article VIII.

races.title: Charter amendment banning data centers over 25 MW
races.target_project: Amazon Data Services campus (~$2B) in the city technology park
races.summary: Adds Article XI, Section 11.05 to the city charter prohibiting construction of data centers with aggregate monthly demand or peak electrical load over 25 MW. Self-executing. Council enacted a moratorium through Jan 31, 2027 while the vote is pending.
races.ballot_text: Proposed Charter Amendment, City of Sunbury. A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. The proposed amendment would amend the Charter of the City of Sunbury to add Section 11.05 to Article XI to read as follows: Article XI, Section 11.05: Prohibition of Construction of a Data Center. (A) The construction of a data center is hereby prohibited. (B) As used in this Section, "construction" shall mean the erection of one or more buildings, infrastructure, facilities, and related activities, which include preparations and modifications for same, for a common purpose. (C) As used in this Section, "data center" shall mean one or more buildings or physical facilities or infrastructure, located on a single real property parcel or on contiguous, adjacent, or otherwise aggregated real property parcels that: (1) Are used primarily or exclusively for digital information services such as the management, storage, processing, and dissemination of electronic data and information through the use of computer systems, servers, networking equipment, and related components, including equipment cooling systems; and (2) Has an aggregate monthly demand or peak load of greater than twenty-five (25) megawatts, however derived from any energy source, or a combination thereof. (D) This Section is self-executing. Shall Article XI, Section 11.05 of the Charter of the City of Sunbury be adopted? YES / NO
races.notes: Delaware County Issue 9 is a different Sunbury charter amendment (council seats); confirm this measure's issue number. Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file (misspelled Sunsbury) as Charter Amendment: Article XI, Section XI. Full text from the Delaware County sample ballot (Sunbury City A), printed without an issue number.

races.title: Charter amendment banning data centers over 25 MW
races.target_project: No formal proposal (M2 Development feasibility study at Conneaut East Industrial Park)
races.opponents: City Manager Nick Sanford warned of judicial review
races.summary: Adds Article XVI, Conservation of Natural Resources, to the city charter, prohibiting data centers with aggregate monthly demand or peak load over 25 MW (318 valid signatures). Council declined to adopt a moratorium; the petition went forward anyway.
races.ballot_text: Issue 10. Proposed Charter Amendment, Conneaut City. A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Shall the Charter of the City of Conneaut be amended to add Article XVI to read as follows: ARTICLE XVI CONSERVATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES. Section XVI-1. Prohibition of Construction of a Data Center. (A) The construction of a data center is hereby prohibited. (B) As used in this Section, "construction" shall mean the erection of one or more buildings, infrastructure, facilities, and related activities, which include preparations and modifications for same, for a common purpose. (C) As used in this Section, "data center" shall mean one or more buildings or physical facilities or infrastructure, located on a single real property parcel or on contiguous, adjacent, or otherwise aggregated real property parcels that (1) Are used primarily or exclusively for digital information services such as the management, storage, processing, and dissemination of electronic data and information through the use of computer systems, servers, networking equipment, and related components, including equipment cooling systems; and (2) Has an aggregate monthly demand or peak load of greater than twenty five (25) megawatts, however derived from any energy source, or a combination thereof. (D) This Section is self-executing. Shall the proposed charter amendment be adopted? YES / NO.
races.notes: NOT present in the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3 Local Questions and Issues file (the only Ashtabula County Conneaut row is a park district levy); the measure is confirmed by the Ashtabula County BOE's Aug 26 approval and News 5 Cleveland. Confirmed as Issue 10 on the Ashtabula County sample ballot for Conneaut precinct 1-C (generated Sept 15, 2026; docs/source-docs/ashtabula-county-sample-ballot-conneaut-1c.pdf), which carries the full Article XVI text.

races.title: Charter amendment banning data centers over 25 MW
races.target_project: Proposed ~600-acre Amazon campus (Madison/St. Clair townships); existing AWS site unaffected
races.summary: Adds Article IX, Section 9.06 to the charter: data center construction is prohibited where aggregate monthly demand or peak load exceeds 25 MW from any energy source or combination; self-executing. Council refused to certify the petition until the Ohio Supreme Court ordered it onto the ballot (State ex rel. Blankenship v. Trenton City Council, 2026-Ohio-3406). Council has teed up a property-tax holiday contingent on the measure failing, and litigation is expected if it passes.
races.ballot_text: Proposed Charter Amendment. A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. Article IX, Section 9.06, Prohibition of Construction of a Data Center: (A) "The construction of a data center is hereby prohibited." (B) "As used in this Section, 'construction' shall mean the erection of one or more buildings, infrastructure, facilities, and related activities [...]" (C) a data center is one or more buildings, physical facilities or infrastructure on a single parcel "or on contiguous, adjacent, or otherwise aggregated real property parcels" that is used primarily for digital information services and "(2) Has an aggregate monthly demand or peak load of greater than twenty five (25) megawatts" from any energy source or combination. (D) "This Section is self-executing." (Per WVXU and the Journal-News reproducing the Butler County ballot text; the "Shall Article IX..." question line was not captured.)
races.notes: Ohio Supreme Court ordered the measure onto the ballot Sept 1, 2026. Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file as Charter Amendment: Article IX, Section 9.06.

races.title: Community Consent Amendment (voter approval for large developments)
races.target_project: ~300-acre data center proposal (Beatty/Rensch Rd)
races.summary: Creates a mandatory public referendum for any development of 50 or more acres, more than 20 MW peak demand, or more than 500,000 gallons of water per day, with the developer paying election costs. Not a ban, but it would subject the proposed data center to a citywide vote. City moratorium runs through June 2027.
races.ballot_text: Issue 28, Community Consent Amendment (Franklin County Board of Elections). Full text of the proposed charter amendment (petition C-37-26, Exhibit A): a Heavy Industrial Development is any development that occupies 50 or more contiguous acres, draws more than 20 megawatts of electrical power at peak capacity, or consumes more than 500,000 gallons of water per day, aggregating phased developments and commonly owned parcels; no such development may be approved without a Public Referendum of city voters, paid for by the applicant through a Referendum Fund, and approved projects are held to Community Impact Standards for noise, infrasound, light and vibration, with new votes required for material changes. (The certified ballot question line itself is not printed in the fetched documents.)
races.notes: Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file as Charter Amendment: XI. Full text of the amendment fetched Oct 16 from the county's 2026 election page (docs/source-docs/grove-city-issue-28-full-text.pdf); the county link named Grove-City-Charter-Amendment-5 serves a 2017 notice of election and is unrelated.

races.title: Charter amendment banning data centers over 25 MW

races.ballot_text: CITY OF PATASKALA Charter Amendment. Shall Section 11.09 (Prohibitation of a Data Center) be added therby prohibiting the constuction of a data center within the City limits? (Verbatim from the Licking County Board of Elections filed-issues list, typos included. races.notes: The Licking County BOE summary shows no megawatt threshold; news reports describe the 25 MW definition. One of four Pataskala charter amendments plus a library levy on the same ballot. Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file as Charter Amendment: Article XI, Section 11.09 (three other Pataskala charter amendments are on the same ballot). Question confirmed against the Licking County issues list (8 precincts).

races.title: Charter amendment capping data centers at 25 MW
races.target_project: Proposed data center on farmland in Oregon
races.summary: Writes a 25 MW cap into the city charter using the Conserve Ohio template. Organizers frame it as steering development to brownfield and industrial sites.
races.ballot_text: Issue 25. Shall the Charter of the City of Oregon be amended to add Section 8 to Article XIII to read as follows? Article XIII, Section 8; Prohibition of Construction of a Data Center. (A) The construction of a data center is hereby prohibited. (B) As used in this Section, "construction" shall mean the erection of one or more buildings, infrastructure, facilities, and related activities, which include preparations and modifications for the same, for a common purpose. (C) As used in this Section, "data center" shall mean one or more buildings or physical facilities or infrastructure, located on a single property parcel or on contiguous, adjacent, or otherwise aggregated real property parcels that: (1) Are used primarily or exclusively for digital information services such as the management, storage, processing, and dissemination of electronic data and information through the use of computing systems, servers, networking equipment, and related components, including equipment cooling systems; and (2) Has an aggregate monthly demand or peak load of greater than twenty-five (25) megawatts, however derived from any energy source, or combination thereof. (D) This section is self-executing. Per the city: a YES vote is in support of the charter change and prohibition of data centers greater than 25 MW; a NO vote is in opposition.
races.notes: Issue 25 (Issues 26 and 27 on the Oregon ballot are unrelated charter changes). Council accepted the BOE certification Aug 19. Lucas County reports on the SOS-hosted ENR platform (Nov 2025 was instance 21). Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file as Charter Amendment: Article XIII, Section 8. Full text from the city's 2026 Election for Voters page.

races.title: Advisory question on allowing data center development
races.target_project: Decimal Digital AI data center pitch
races.summary: Non-binding advisory question from Village Council asking whether residents support allowing data center development within village limits, subject to zoning and development agreements. The ballot itself says the result will not, by itself, approve or prohibit any specific project. The village adopted a 12-month moratorium in February after Decimal Digital's pitch and is still owed about $1.3M from a 2024 crypto-mining operation.
races.ballot_text: Advisory Election, Village of Monroeville. A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. The purpose of this advisory question is to provide Village Council with public input, realizing the result will not, by itself, approve or prohibit any specific data center project. Do you support the Village of Monroeville allowing data center development within the Village limits, provided such development complies with Village zoning regulations and applicable development agreements? YES / NO.
races.notes: A YES vote favors allowing data centers. The Huron County sample ballot for Monroeville Village (generated Sept 3, 2026; docs/source-docs/huron-county-sample-ballot-monroeville-village.pdf) prints this as an ADVISORY ELECTION with the question above, so the earlier reporting was right and the Ohio Secretary of State file's one-line description ("Shall the proposed ordinance allowing data center development be adopted?") does not match the ballot. Placed by Village Council (the question is addressed to council for public input). No issue number is printed.

races.title: Adopt township zoning to regulate a data center at the Stuart plant site
races.target_project: Data center at the former J.M. Stuart power plant site (federal permit issued)
races.summary: Township zoning adoption under ORC Chapter 519, which requires voter approval. Adopting zoning gives the township authority over the proposed data center at the former Stuart power plant; trustees passed a one-year voluntary moratorium in March.
races.ballot_text: Proposed Zoning Plan, Township of Sprigg. A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. A Resolution enacted under Section 519 of the Ohio Revised Code, titled "Sprigg Township Zoning Resolution", governing the unincorporated area of Sprigg Township, Adams County, Ohio, to preserve the rural and agricultural character of the Township, protect public health, safety, and general welfare, allow reasonable use of property with minimal unnecessary regulation, provide a predictable process for review of higher-impact development, ensure that uses with potentially significant impacts are evaluated and reasonably mitigated, and to promote orderly and compatible land use consistent with Township infrastructure and services. Pursuant to the authority conferred by Section 519 of the Ohio Revised Code, and for the purpose of protecting agricultural, residential, and small-scale uses; preventing unreasonable burdens on roads, infrastructure, and public services; providing uniform and objective standards for land use review; and to carry out zoning authority in a manner consistent with Ohio law. Shall the zoning plan for the unincorporated area of the Township of Sprigg as adopted by the Township of Sprigg be approved? For the Zoning Resolution / Against the Zoning Resolution.
races.notes: Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file as Sprigg Township, Zoning amendment. Full ballot text from the Adams County sample ballot for Sprigg Township (generated Oct 12, 2026; docs/source-docs/adams-county-sample-ballot-sprigg-township.pdf). The ballot choices are For the Zoning Resolution / Against the Zoning Resolution, not Yes / No. The question says the plan was adopted by the township (trustees' zoning resolution under ORC 519, which goes to the voters under ORC 519.11), so the origin is the township board rather than a petition. No issue number is printed.

races.title: Referendum on Resolution 06-2026 (EdgeConneX development agreement)
races.target_project: EdgeConneX: two data centers and a gas plant on ~195 acres
races.proponents: Teays Valley Community Alliance (petition, 669 valid signatures)
races.summary: Referendum on the council's April resolution approving a development and supply agreement term summary with EdgeConneX. The Ohio Supreme Court ordered the petition certified (State ex rel. McNamara-Smith v. Grube, 2026-Ohio-3035). A YES vote upholds the agreement; a NO vote rejects it (though it does not by itself stop construction). EdgeConneX paid the village $3.5M in October.
races.ballot_text: Referendum on Resolution (By Petition), Village of Ashville. A majority affirmative vote is necessary for passage. WHEREAS, EdgeConneX intends to obtain permits through the Village of Ashville to construct and operate two data center buildings with ancillary buildings and infrastructure on certain property within the Village (currently Pickaway County Parcel Number D1300350000100 consisting of approximately 195.368 acres); and WHEREAS, EdgeConneX, through an affiliate, also intends to develop and obtain permits through the Ohio Power Siting Board for authority to construct and operate a natural gas behind-the-meter power generating facility at the property; and WHEREAS, the Village of Ashville and EdgeConneX want to memorialize a framework and timeline, for disclosure of Energy Center parameters, studies, and EdgeConneX's paid support to the Village, the Township, and the School District, through a Term Summary; and WHEREAS, using this Term Summary, the Village of Ashville and EdgeConneX will negotiate and agree to a Development and Supply Agreement that must be approved by Council for the Village of Ashville; and WHEREAS, Council for the Village of Ashville now wants to kick off this project by approving the Term Summary. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the Village of Ashville, County of Pickaway, State of Ohio: Section One. Council for the Village of Ashville hereby approves the Development and Supply Agreement Term Summary attached hereto as Exhibit A. Section Two. It is hereby found and determined that all formal actions of this Council concerning and relating to the passage of this resolution were adopted in an open meeting of Council and all deliberations of Council and any of the decision-making bodies of the Village of Ashville which resulted in such formal actions were taken in meetings open to the public in compliance with all legal requirements of the State of Ohio. Section Three. All prior legislation, or any parts thereof, which is/are inconsistent with this Resolution is/are hereby repealed as to the inconsistent parts thereof. Section Four. Council declares this to be an emergency measure immediately necessary for the preservation of the public peace, health, and safety of this municipality and for the further reason that Council needs to accept these terms as soon as possible so that this project is not unnecessarily delayed. Wherefore, provided this Resolution receives the required affirmative votes of Council, this Resolution shall take effect and be in force immediately upon passage by Council. Shall the resolution enacting approval of a development and supply agreement term summary with EdgeConneX be approved? Yes / No.
races.notes: A YES vote is the pro-data-center side. Ballot choices are Yes / No (not For / Against), per the Pickaway County ballot proof for precinct 17 Ashville-East (docs/source-docs/pickaway-county-ballot-proof-ashville-east-p2.webp), which prints the full resolution text above the question. Council's attempt to repeal the agreement (Resolution 16-2026) failed at its third reading on Oct 5, 2026, so the referendum stays on the ballot. Village electors only. Listed on the Ohio Secretary of State's Nov 3, 2026 Local Questions and Issues file with the same question wording. No issue number is printed.

races.title: Ban on high-impact data centers in all zoning districts
races.target_project: Proposed data center bid (~$3M, funding source contested in court)
races.opponents: Regional Development Association of East Central Kansas; city staff
races.summary: Citizen-initiated ordinance (K.S.A. 12-3013) prohibiting the construction, installation, operation and maintenance of High Impact Data Centers in every zoning district. A High Impact Data Center is one with peak electrical load over 10 MW or daily water draw over 100,000 gallons, including server farms, colocation, AI training and crypto mining. A district court ordered the question onto the ballot; the city's declaratory-judgment case on whether the subject is a proper initiative is still pending, so if approved the ordinance takes effect only after a ruling. Companion Question #3 would ban large battery storage.
races.ballot_text: Ballot Question 2: An Ordinance of the City of Emporia, Kansas Prohibiting the Installation and Operation of High Impact Data Centers. Explanatory Statement: This ordinance would prohibit the construction, installation, operation, and maintenance of High Impact Data Centers within the City of Emporia, Kansas. A "High Impact Data Center" is defined as a facility whose primary purpose is the housing, operation, and maintenance of computer servers and related infrastructure that requires a peak electrical load exceeding ten (10) megawatts or a daily water draw exceeding one hundred thousand (100,000) gallons. This term includes server farms, colocation facilities, AI training facilities, cryptocurrency mining operations, and similar high-density computing facilities. The prohibition would apply to all zoning districts within the City. Violations would be subject to civil and criminal penalties under the City of Emporia Zoning Regulations. Shall the following ordinance be adopted? "An Ordinance of the City of Emporia, Kansas Prohibiting the Installation and Operation of High Impact Data Centers" Vote Yes to adopt the ordinance. Vote No to reject the ordinance.
races.notes: Polls close 7 pm Central. Ballot Question 2 (form of ballot per Resolution 3799, Exhibit B); Question 3 is the companion battery-storage ban. A YES vote adopts the ordinance. Resolution 3799 (adopted Aug 26, 2026; docs/source-docs/emporia-resolution-3799.pdf) records that the Lyon County District Court ordered the question onto the ballot on Aug 20, 2026 (case LY-2026-CV-000119) and stayed publication, implementation and enforcement of the ordinance pending final judgment regardless of the outcome, while the city preserves its argument that the subject is administrative and not a proper initiative. The Emporia Gazette reports the petition text cites a nonexistent code article.

races.title: Ten-year ban on high-impact data centers and large battery storage
races.target_project: Possible data center project discussed in April 2026
races.opponents: City of El Dorado (lost court challenge)
races.summary: Citizen-initiated ordinance prohibiting High Impact Data Centers and Tier 2 and Tier 3 battery energy storage systems. Under K.S.A. 12-3013, if adopted by voters it cannot be amended or repealed by the commission for ten years without voter approval. The 13th Judicial District court ruled the petition a proper legislative subject (Aug 21, 2026 city statement); the City Commission placed it on the ballot by resolution at a special meeting on Aug 25, 2026.
races.ballot_text: Shall the following ordinance be adopted? [ordinance title] prohibiting the installation and operation of High Impact Data Centers and Tier 2 and Tier 3 Battery Energy Storage Systems. Per the city's Aug 26, 2026 official statement, the question as approved by the City Commission carries the ordinance title, the specific technical thresholds defining "High Impact Data Center" (peak electrical load exceeding 10 megawatts or a daily water draw exceeding 100,000 gallons) and "Tier 2 and Tier 3 Battery Energy Storage Systems" (Tier 2: aggregate capacity between 81 and 600 kilowatt-hours or more than one storage technology in a room or enclosed area; Tier 3: over 600 kilowatt-hours), and a description of the ordinance's ten-year effective period, under the "generally descriptive" option in K.S.A. 12-3013(b). (Reconstructed from city notices 652, 683 and 688 and the Aug 26 statement; the certified question text as printed on the Butler County ballot has not been retrieved.)
races.notes: Polls close 7 pm Central. Results page URL unverified. The 13th Judicial District ruled in August that the ordinance is legislative and may proceed by initiative (city notice 683); the commission's Aug 26, 2026 official statement on the ballot question is in docs/source-docs/el-dorado-ks-official-statement-ballot-question-2026-08-26.pdf and says the full ordinance will be published on eldoks.gov under K.S.A. 12-3013(d). The sample ballot from the Butler County Clerk (bucoks.gov Elections) would give the verbatim question.

races.title: Allow data centers in the Eldorado Valley Transfer Area
races.target_project: Roughly 14,000 acres of city-owned desert outside the tortoise habitat easement
races.summary: City Charter section 144(1) limits land uses in the Eldorado Valley Transfer Area (over 100,000 acres bought from the federal government in 1995, of which over 86,000 acres sit under a habitat conservation easement) and section 144(2) requires voter approval of any new use. A YES vote makes data centers an approved land use on the roughly 14,000 acres outside the easement; individual leases would still need council approval, and lease proceeds would be split under Charter section 142.3. The city says the measure does not change existing law or raise taxes. Uses outside the Transfer Area are not affected.
races.ballot_text: Should data center facilities be an approved land use within the Eldorado Valley Transfer Area outside of the Multi-species Habitat Conservation Easement? Yes / No. From the city's Explanation and Digest: "A YES vote would allow data center facilities to be an approved land use within the Eldorado Valley Transfer Area outside of the Multi-species Habitat Conservation Easement. A NO vote would mean that no data center facilities would be approved within the Eldorado Valley Transfer Area outside of the Multi-species Habitat Conservation Easement." If approved, the City Council would only be authorized to potentially enter into leases allowing data center facilities; voter approval of the use would not require the City Council to authorize a data center.
races.notes: A YES vote is the pro-data-center side. Polls close 7 pm Pacific. Question, explanation and digest verbatim from the city Explanation and Digest (docs/source-docs/boulder-city-q1-digest.pdf); the Clark County all-questions booklet (docs/source-docs/clark-county-all-questions-26g.pdf) adds the ballot question committees' arguments for and against passage. Amends the Charter to prohibit the approval, construction, expansion, or operation of new data centers within the City; prohibits the City from issuing development approvals or permits authorizing such facilities; defines "data center"; and requires voter approval before the Charter prohibition may be amended or repealed. Should the City Charter prohibit new data centers within the City? Yes, in favor of adoption. No, against adoption.
races.notes: Polls close 7 pm Eastern (Volusia is in the Eastern zone). The amendment is one of seven charter questions the council sent to the ballot Aug 3, 2026. races.title: Bond and noise guarantee for hyperscale data centers seeking tax breaks
races.target_project: Province Group proposal (village declined its abatement/PILOT request in July)
races.summary: Citizen-initiated ordinance requiring any hyperscale data center developer (over 10,000 sq ft, over 5,000 servers, or over 50 MW) that seeks a tax abatement, PILOT or other special tax designation to first deposit a bond or escrow equal to at least the projected tax revenue over the project's 31-year life plus projected salaries for 200 full-time employees, with annual make-whole payments if projections fall short and assessments for environmental, standard-of-living or property-value effects. Also requires a noise guarantee of 50 dB by day and 45 dB overnight with council-set fines. Conditions the deal rather than banning the building.
races.ballot_text: Shall the ordinance amending Chapter 133.01 "Established; Power & Duties" of the codified ordinances of the Village of Perry be adopted? (Ohio Secretary of State listing; Lake County Issue 16.) Full text (initiative petition, Form 6-I): amends Codified Ordinances section 133.01(c)(23) so that before the Fiscal Officer signs any village agreement granting tax abatements, PILOT programs or any special tax designation to a hyperscale data center (one that exceeds 10,000 square feet, 5,000 servers or 50 megawatts), the developer must first deposit a Data Center Bond of no less than the projected tax revenues over the proposed 31-year life of the property plus the value of 200 full-time salaries projected across 31 years; annual shortfalls against employment or tax projections are paid to residents, the remaining principal is returned to the developer after 31 years, and any abatement applicant must guarantee a maximum of 50 dBA by day (6:30 am to 10:00 pm) and 45 dBA at night, with fines set by council.
races.notes: Found Oct 15 as the jurisdiction missing from the earlier list; with Piqua (moved to Feb 2027) it reconciles Ballotpedia's 21 measures / 18 jurisdictions. Confirmed as Issue 16 on the Lake County certified issues list (docs/source-docs/lake-county-issues-11-3-26.pdf); full ordinance text fetched Oct 16 (docs/source-docs/perry-village-ordinance-full-text.pdf, scanned petition, OCR applied).
